translation: The mathematical sciences are not true sciences.
translation_note: A short, unqualified thesis; Farmer groups it with 7>2-5 as a set (farmer1998:23698).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch15, from Latin at farmer1998:23613
attribution: Pico's own opinion, among the mathematical conclusions (section 7>, farmer1998:23606).

sources.text: the fourteenth-century calculatores (Bradwardine, Swineshead, Buridan, Oresme)
sources.pico_relation: Farmer identifies these as the 'moderns' targeted across theses 7>1-5

doctrine: The thesis states, without qualification, that the mathematical sciences are not true sciences (farmer1998:23613). Farmer groups it with 7>2-5 as a set, and identifies the 'moderns' targeted across the set as the fourteenth-century calculatores, Bradwardine, Swineshead, Buridan, and Oresme, who applied mathematics to problems that Aristotelian physics had treated qualitatively (farmer1998:23698).
context: Farmer states that the traditional claim that Renaissance Platonism helped promote the mathematical physics of the later Scientific Revolution finds little support in these theses, especially in 7>5 (farmer1998:23698).
historiography: Cassirer cites this thesis together with the following two mathematical conclusions as denying that mathematics is a true science, on the ground that 'a supersensible knowledge, which is alone able to disclose the supersensible nature' of things is distinct from mathematical knowledge (cassirer1942:1133).

quotations.text: a supersensible knowledge, which is alone able to disclose the supersensible nature

not_established: Farmer's fuller argument for why these theses give little support to the Platonism-promoted-mathematical-physics thesis, beyond the one-line summary consulted, is not established here (farmer1998:23698).
